text: A company runs a five-minute nightly reporting job on an Amazon EC2 instance. It rewrites the job as an AWS Lambda function that uses a managed runtime. Which task does the company no longer have to do?

options.text: Writing and testing the code of the report job
Patching the operating system that the job runs on
Granting the job IAM permissions to read its data
Protecting the report files that the job saves to S3

explanation: With Lambda there are no servers for the customer to manage, so AWS patches the operating system and, for managed runtimes, applies runtime updates. The function code, its IAM permissions and the data it writes remain the customer's responsibility.

text: A company stores application logs in Amazon S3. The logs are read often for 30 days and almost never afterward, but must be kept for 7 years. Retrieval of old logs can take hours. Which solution meets these needs with the LEAST cost and effort?

options.text: Keep the logs in S3 Standard and turn on S3 Versioning for them
Copy the logs each month to Amazon EBS Cold HDD volumes by hand
Move the logs each month to Amazon EFS with a manual script
Add an S3 Lifecycle rule that moves logs to S3 Glacier Deep Archive

explanation: An S3 Lifecycle rule moves objects automatically, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost class for long-term archives that can wait hours for retrieval. Keeping everything in S3 Standard costs more, and the EBS and EFS options add manual work and higher storage prices.

text: A company runs its application in a primary AWS Region with a standby copy in a second Region. Its Amazon RDS database must fail over automatically if its Availability Zone fails, and users must be sent to the second Region if the primary Region stops passing health checks. Which features meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: An Amazon RDS Multi-AZ deployment
An RDS read replica in the same Availability Zone
Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing
Amazon Route 53 failover routing with health checks
Amazon ElastiCache in front of the database

explanation: A Multi-AZ deployment keeps a standby in another Availability Zone and fails over to it automatically, and Route 53 failover routing sends users to the standby Region when health checks show the primary is down. A read replica serves reads and must be promoted by hand, and geolocation routing chooses by user location, not by health.

text: A company runs a web application in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. When average CPU utilization stays above 70%, it wants more instances to be added automatically and the operations team to get an email. What should the company set up?

options.text: A CloudWatch alarm that triggers scaling and an SNS topic
An AWS CloudTrail trail that sends API logs to Amazon S3
AWS Trusted Advisor performance checks with weekly emails
An AWS Config rule that checks the instance type in use

explanation: An Amazon CloudWatch alarm watches the CPU metric and, when it changes state, can run an EC2 Auto Scaling action and notify an Amazon SNS topic that emails the team. CloudTrail records API calls and Config checks configurations; neither reacts to CPU load.

text: A company has 12 AWS accounts. Finance wants a single bill for all accounts, and the security team wants to stop every account from using AWS Regions outside Europe, even if an IAM policy in the account allows it. Which actions meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create IAM user groups for each team in the management account
Use consolidated billing in AWS Organizations
Turn on AWS Cost Explorer forecasts in each account
Buy AWS Business Support+ for every account
Attach a service control policy that denies other Regions

explanation: AWS Organizations consolidated billing gives one bill for all member accounts, and a service control policy (SCP) sets the maximum permissions for the member accounts it applies to, so it can block other Regions even when IAM allows them. SCPs do not restrict the management account. IAM groups only apply inside one account, and Cost Explorer analyzes spending without restricting anything.

text: A security audit finds that some Amazon EC2 instances may run software with known vulnerabilities. The company wants to scan the instances continuously and then install operating system patches across hundreds of instances. Which AWS services should it use? (Choose two.)

options.text: Amazon Inspector
Amazon Macie
AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager
Amazon GuardDuty

explanation: Amazon Inspector continuously scans EC2 instances for known software vulnerabilities, and Systems Manager Patch Manager installs patches at scale; patching the guest OS is the customer's job under the shared responsibility model. Session Manager opens shell sessions but does not patch, GuardDuty detects threats from activity logs rather than scanning software, and Macie finds sensitive data in S3.

text: A company builds an internal assistant with Amazon Bedrock that answers questions from the company's documents. Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which task belongs to the company?

options.text: Maintaining the servers that run the foundation models
Patching the virtualization layer of the Bedrock hosts
Controlling who can access the documents and the assistant
Protecting the physical data centers where Bedrock runs

explanation: With a managed service such as Amazon Bedrock, AWS protects the infrastructure, including servers, virtualization and data centers. The customer remains responsible for its data and for access control, for example with IAM permissions.

text: A company wants to stop paying for Oracle licenses by moving its on-premises Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. The database must stay online for users while the data is copied. Which approach should the company use?

options.text: Rehost the database server on EC2 with AWS Transform MGN
Copy the database files to Amazon S3 with AWS DataSync
Back up the database nightly with AWS Backup and restore it
Convert the schema with DMS Schema Conversion, then use DMS

explanation: A heterogeneous move needs the schema converted first (DMS Schema Conversion or AWS SCT), and AWS DMS then copies the data while the source keeps running. Rehosting with AWS Transform MGN would keep running Oracle on EC2, so the license cost would remain.

text: Application servers in a private subnet must download operating system updates from the internet, but the internet must not be able to start connections to them. Only members of the network team may change the VPC route tables. Which setup meets these requirements?

options.text: Add an internet gateway route and give all developers AdministratorAccess
Give the servers public IP addresses and let every IAM user edit routes
Use a NAT gateway and allow route changes only for the network team group
Use a NAT gateway and share the root user password with the network team

explanation: A NAT gateway lets private instances start outbound connections while the internet cannot reach them, and an IAM policy attached to the network team's group grants route table changes only to those who need them (least privilege). Sharing root credentials or granting everyone broad access breaks IAM best practices, and an internet gateway route or public IP addresses expose the servers.

text: An auditor asks a company for AWS's SOC 2 report and for proof that the company itself controls the encryption keys of its Amazon S3 data, including the ability to disable them. What should the company do?

options.text: Request the report from AWS Support and use SSE-S3 keys
Get the report from AWS Artifact and use KMS customer managed keys
Get the report from AWS Artifact and use SSE-S3 encryption keys
Generate the report with AWS Config and use AWS managed keys

explanation: AWS Artifact provides AWS's SOC reports on demand, and AWS KMS customer managed keys let the company set the key policy, rotation and disabling. SSE-S3 keys and AWS managed keys are managed by AWS, so the company cannot disable them, and AWS Config does not produce SOC reports.
